name: vwap_anchored_support_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Anchored VWAP from significant prior events (earnings release, 52-week high/low, large gap day) acts as a persistent institutional memory of fair value from that event. When current price approaches an anchored VWAP from a major event, institutional participants who entered near that event face break-even decisions, creating supply/demand clusters. The inefficiency exists because standard platforms only show session VWAP, not anchored VWAP from arbitrary dates. Traders who compute anchored VWAP gain an informational edge over those using only session VWAP. The edge persists because most retail traders lack the data infrastructure to compute multi-day anchored VWAPs efficiently.
mechanism: VWAP is the institutional execution benchmark. When spot deviates significantly from session VWAP, algorithmic execution engines increase order flow to mean-revert their fills toward VWAP. This creates measurable gravitational pull, especially during lower-volume mid-session periods when fewer competing flows are present.

exit.signal_exit: exit if price recrosses anchored_VWAP against the position direction

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; anchored levels are less reliable in panic regimes

weaknesses: Requires maintaining a calendar of events and computing multi-day anchored VWAPs — significant data engineering overhead
Anchored VWAP levels that are too old (>30 days) lose their institutional memory relevance
Signal is rare — only triggers when price approaches a specific level, may have 0 trade days frequently
prior_art: Anchored VWAP was popularized by Brian Shannon ('Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes') and is available on TradingView. Institutional use of anchored VWAP is discussed by DeMark and others. The concept of event-based anchoring adds specificity beyond generic anchored VWAP.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
